title: Lipidomic analysis of cells and tissues
author: Annie Jen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.byn2pvge
materials: Maintain the prepared sample solutions at 4°C prior to analysis via LC-MS/MS.

The resulting LC–MS/MS data is processed using Compound Discoverer 2.1 or higher (Thermo Scientific) and LipiDex [3] , an in-house-developed software suite. The LipiDex software and tutorials can be found at https://github.com/coongroup/LipiDex. [3] Hutchins, P., Russell, J., Coon, J.: LipiDex: An Integrated Software Package for High-Confidence Lipid Identification. Cell Systems. 6(5): 621-625. doi: 10.1016/j.cels.2018.03.011

MS acquisition will be performed with a Thermo Scientific heated electrospray ionization (HESI II) probe in Ion Max API source housing operating in both positive and negative mode. Source parameters should be set as follows: capillary temperature at 350 °C, sheath gas flow rate at 25 units, aux gas flow rate at 15 units, sweep gas flow rate at 5 units, spray voltage at |3.5 kV|, and S-lens RF at 90.0 units. The MS should be operated in a polarity switching mode acquiring positive and negative full MS1 scans followed by data-dependent MS2 spectra (Top2) within the same injection, using the exclusion list in Appendix 1. Data acquisition for full MS1 scans in both modes should be collected at 30,000 resolution, 1 × 10 6 automatic gain control (AGC) target, 100 ms ion accumulation time (max IT), and 200 to 2000 m/z scan range. Data dependent (dd-MS2) scans in both modes should be collected at 30,000 resolution, 1 × 10 5 AGC target, 50 ms max IT, 1.0 m/z isolation window, and stepped normalized collision energy (NCE) at 20, 30, 40, with a 10.0 s dynamic exclusion.

steps.title: Prepare Plasma Samples
steps.instruction: Thaw plasma samples on ice. Transfer 10 µL into a 1.5 mL microfuge tube and maintain on ice throughout the extraction.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Samples
steps.instruction: Pulverize tissue samples into a fine powder using a ceramic mortar and pestle cooled with liquid nitrogen. Weigh approximately 15 mg of the frozen pulverized tissue into a 1.5 mL polypropylene microcentrifuge tube and record the 'frozen wet weight'. Ensure samples remain frozen throughout the process.

steps.title: Prepare Purified Organelles
steps.instruction: Wash purified organelles (e.g., mitochondria, nuclei, lysosomes, endosomes) with a low-salt or ammoniated buffer (e.g., 100 mM ammonium acetate) compatible with electrospray ionization. If using magnetic beads for immunopurification, organelles can be extracted directly from the beads without elution.

steps.title: Prepare Cell Pellets
steps.instruction: Ensure a minimum of 10x10^6 cells are present in the pellet. If the frozen cell pellet is already washed and supernatant removed, proceed directly to extraction. If washing is required, follow these steps:

substeps.instruction: Chill a vial of wash solution (e.g., 0.3% ammonium acetate, 0.3% ammonium formate, 0.9% NaCl, 1 M PBS, or 100 mM HEPES).
Add 1 mL wash to the pellet and resuspend by pipetting up and down.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 2 minutes at 4°C and decant supernatant.
Repeat washing 2-3 times total.
Allow cell pellet to dry on ice for 5 minutes.
Use immediately or snap freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C.

steps.title: Perform Sample Lysis
steps.instruction: Choose one of the following lysis methods if required for cells, tissues, or organelles; otherwise, vortex for 10 seconds and incubate on ice for at least 10 minutes:

substeps.instruction: Steel beads: Add one 5mm stainless steel bead to a screw-cap tube; bead beat at 25 hz for 5 minutes using a Retsch MM400 mixer mill at 4°C.
Probe sonicator: Sonicate for 10 seconds at 4°C, avoiding excessive heat.
Ultrasonic bath: Sonicate for 5 minutes (20 s pulse-on, 10 s pulse-off, amplitude 30) with water as cool as possible.

steps.title: Perform MTBE Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract lipids using the Matyash method (MTBE/methanol/water proportions 10/3/2.5 v/v/v) in translucent tubes. Chill MTBE, methanol, and water on ice.

substeps.instruction: Add 225 µL chilled methanol to the sample and vortex for 10 seconds.
Add 750 µL chilled MTBE to the sample and vortex for 10 seconds.
Add 187.5 µL chilled water to induce phase separation.
Incubate on ice for at least 10 minutes.
Centrifuge at 14,000 x g for 2 minutes at 4°C.
Visually confirm two layers (upper organic lipid layer and lower aqueous metabolite layer).

steps.title: Recover and Resuspend Lipids
steps.instruction: Isolate the lipid fraction and prepare for LC-MS analysis.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL of the upper organic layer into an autosampler vial with fused glass insert.
Dry down in a vacuum concentrator at ambient temperature.
Add 50 µL Lipid Resuspension Solvent (9:1 MeOH:toluene) to the dried extract.
Cap and vortex for at least 10 seconds.
Briefly centrifuge vials to spin down liquid on the caps.

steps.title: Configure LC-MS System
steps.instruction: Prepare the instrument for sample injection.

substeps.instruction: Purge mobile phase lines to remove air bubbles.
Connect Waters Acquity CSH C18 column and pre-column; verify pressure and check for leaks.
Perform MS evaluations and mass calibrations.

steps.title: Run LC-MS Analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 10 µL of sample. Separate at a constant flow rate of 0.4 mL/min at 50°C using the following gradient: 0-2 min 2%B, 2-5 min 2%B, 5-30 min 5%B, 6-50 min 5%B, 20-85 min 5%B, 21-99 min 5%B, 28-99 min 5%B, 28.25-2 min 5%B, 30-2 min 5%B.

steps.title: Process Raw Data
steps.instruction: Convert raw data files to centroid and .mgf format using Proteowizard msConvertGUI.

steps.title: Identify Lipids via LipiDex
steps.instruction: Use the Spectrum Searcher module in LipiDex to identify lipids.

substeps.instruction: Add .mgf files and use the 'Lipidex_HCD_acetate' library.
Set MS1 Search Tolerance, MS2 Search Tolerance, Max Search Results Returned, and MS2 Low Mass Cutoff.
Select 'Search Spectra' to generate results in the input directory.
Filter spectral matches using a dot product score > 500 and reverse dot product score > 700.

steps.title: Generate Aligned Feature Table
steps.instruction: Create an aligned workflow in Compound Discoverer.

substeps.instruction: Start 'New Study and Analysis', add all .raw files, and identify blank matrix files.
Build workflow: Input Files → Select Spectra → Align Retention Times → Detect Unknown Compounds → Group Unknown Compounds → Fill Gaps → Mark Background Compounds.

Apply specific node parameters: Select Spectra (Precursor MS(n-1), RT 0.2-21, Mass 100-5000 Da, S/N 1.5); Align RT (Adaptive Curve, Max Shift 0.6, Mass Tol 7.5); Detect Unknowns (Mass Tol 10ppm, Int Tol 100%, S/N 3, Min Peak Int 500,000, Max Element C100 H190 N10 Na2 O15 P2 S2); Group Unknowns (Mass Tol 10, RT Tol 0.5); Fill Gaps (Mass Tol 10, S/N 3); Mark Background (Max Sample/Blank 3).
Run analysis, open results, and export to Excel (Levels 1: Compounds, 2: Compounds per File, 3: Features).
Save as .csv.

steps.title: Generate Unaligned Feature Table
steps.instruction: Create an unaligned workflow in the same Compound Discoverer study.

substeps.instruction: Build workflow: Input Files → Select Spectra → Detect Unknown Compounds using the same parameters as the aligned workflow.
Run analysis, open results, and export to Excel (Level 1: Features, Levels 2-3 blank).
Save as .csv.

steps.title: Final Peak Filtering in LipiDex
steps.instruction: Integrate data in the LipiDex Peak Finder module.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Compound Discoverer' as peak table type.
Upload aligned and unaligned .csv peak feature tables.
Upload MS/MS result .csv files via Results Uploader; ensure positive/negative polarity experiments share the same File ID.
Update MS/MS filtering: Min. Lipid Spectral Purity, Min. MS2 Search Dot Product, Min. MS2 Search Rev. Dot Product, FWHM Window Multiplier, and Max. Mass Difference.
Update Result Filtering: Max. RT M.A.D. Factor (default 3.5) and Feature Found in n Files (default 1).
Select 'Identify Chromatographic Peaks' to generate Final_Results.csv, Unfiltered_Results.csv, and Sample_Information.csv.
